lines.desc: A mechanical stopwatch: the crown starts and stops it, the seconds hand goes round once a minute in 1/5 s steps, and reset flies it back to zero.

lines.name: storage2u
lines.sig: storage2u cx cy k on=0|1 lab=0 lit=chassis|drives|ears|lights
lines.desc: A 2U rack storage server: twelve 3.5-inch drive bays with activity lights across its front, rack ears with handles; the lights blink with disk work. Origin: front mounting face, bottom middle. anchors: top

lines.name: storeshelf
lines.sig: storeshelf cx cy k items=0..8 lab=0 lit=frame|shelves|rails|stock
lines.desc: A freestanding shop shelf unit 100 × 45 × 180 cm: side panels, back panel, kick plate, four shelves with price rails and labels; items 0..8 per shelf shows full stock or scarcity. anchors: top shelf1 shelf2 shelf3 shelf4

lines.name: straightwire
lines.sig: straightwire cx cy k I=-6..6 lab=0 lit=wire|post|card|current
lines.desc: A thick copper rod 25 cm tall standing on a terminal block and passing up through a hole in a white card on four posts (where plotting compasses stand); I sets the current's arrow up or down the rod, B = μ₀I/(2πr) round it. anchors: foot top card

lines.name: string
lines.sig: string cx cy k to=<id>.<anchor> dx=-200..200 dy=-200..200 dz=-200..200 sag=0..1 kind=nylon|thread|cotton knots=0|1 lab=0 lit=line|knots
lines.example: string 300 200 24 dx=16 dy=-4 dz=-6 sag=0.6 kind=cotton lab=1
lines.desc: A length of nylon line, black thread or cotton string from its start to to=<id>.<anchor> (or dx dy dz cm): taut and straight at sag=0, hanging slack up to sag=1, a knot and cut tail at each end; set the end or the sag and it moves there, eased. anchors: end

lines.name: studfinder
lines.sig: studfinder cx cy width scan=1 at=x lab=1 lit=finder|stud|drywall
lines.desc: A stud wall cut open (2×4 studs at 16 in centres behind ½ in drywall) and a stud finder whose LEDs light over the wood as it slides.

lines.name: talljar
lines.sig: talljar cx cy k fill=0..1 lab=0 lit=glass|water
lines.desc: A tall glass jar (8 cm across, 60 cm tall, on a glass foot) of water, for a resonance tube to stand in; a bench part. anchors: rim water inside

lines.name: tapecase
lines.sig: tapecase cx cy k aim=up|right|flat out=0..300 lock=0|1 lab=0 lit=case|tape|hook
lines.desc: A 25 ft tape measure: yellow blade with inch marks (feet in red), a riveted hook, the case with its bumper, lock and belt clip; the hook is the origin and the blade runs out cm up the wall, along it or along a surface to the case. anchors: case

lines.name: tapemeasure
lines.sig: tapemeasure cx cy width out=0-100 lock=0|1 lab=1 lit=case|tape|hook|lock|plank
lines.desc: A tape measure on a plank: the yellow tape pulls out of its case, its hook catches the far end and the marks read 11¾ in; the lock holds it and the spring winds it back.

lines.name: taxform
lines.sig: taxform cx cy k fill=0..1 lab=0 lit=form|fields|signature|payslip|clip
lines.desc: A tax return form on a desk: plain header, name and tax number boxes, four boxed fields (income 32000.00, deductions 4000.00, taxable income 28000.00, tax due at 15 % = 4200.00), a declaration and signature line, a payslip clipped behind it; fill writes the boxes in and signs it. anchors: sign due clip

lines.name: teatpipette
lines.sig: teatpipette cx cy k aim=down|flat fill=0..1 c=clear|blue|red|green|purple|… drops=0..40 fall=1..30 lab=0 lit=bulb|barrel|liquid
lines.desc: A dropper (teat pipette): squeeze the red rubber bulb and drops of about 0.05 mL swell at the glass tip, break off and fall; hangs tip-down over a tube or lies on the bench. anchors: tip top

lines.name: telecomcab
lines.sig: telecomcab cx cy k kind=radio|power lab=0 lit=cabinet|door|vents|plinth
lines.desc: A grey steel outdoor telecom cabinet 80 × 70 × 160 cm on a plinth, door seams, hinges, a lockable handle and vents; radio/baseband, or power with battery backup. anchors: top gland

lines.name: testtube
lines.sig: testtube cx cy length c=red level=0.35 rot=deg lab=1 lit=tube|clamp|stand
lines.desc: A test tube clamped on a stand; tilt it and the liquid stays level with the bench.

lines.name: tuberack
lines.sig: tuberack cx cy width c=red,blue,green,yellow lab=1 lit=tube1|tube2|…|rack
lines.desc: A wooden test-tube rack with a drilled top shelf, holding one tube of each solution.

lines.name: thermometer
lines.sig: thermometer cx cy height level=0.6 temp=… lab=1 lit=thermometer|beaker|burner|tripod|stand
lines.desc: A −10 to 110 °C thermometer in a beaker of water over a Bunsen burner: the column climbs as the water heats and stops at 100 °C while it boils.

lines.name: thermostat
lines.sig: thermostat cx cy size temp=N room=N lab=1 lit=display|up|down|mode|vent
lines.desc: A wall thermostat: below the set point it turns the furnace on (flame on the display, warm air from the register) and off once the room is warm.

lines.name: tidal
lines.sig: tidal cx cy width tide=-1..1 lab=1 lit=rotor|nacelle|tripod|cable
lines.desc: A tidal turbine on a tripod on the seabed, in a clear sea block: the flood tide turns the rotor one way, slack water stops it, the ebb turns it back.

lines.name: tincan
lines.sig: tincan cx cy k label=red|green|yellow|blue lab=0 lit=tin|label|lid
lines.desc: A 400 g food tin, 7.5 × 11 cm: ribbed tinplate body, a plain paper label, a ring-pull lid; a grocery item to price, count or stack on a shelf. anchors: top

lines.name: tire
lines.sig: tire cx cy size k=good|flat psi=0-50 lab=1 lit=tyre|rim|nuts|valve|nail
lines.desc: A wheel on the road; its footprint is load ÷ pressure, so a nail that lets the air out squashes the tyre until the rim nearly sits on the road.

lines.name: tiregauge
lines.sig: tiregauge cx cy size psi=0-60 on=0|1 lab=1 lit=gauge|bar|stem|piston
lines.desc: A pencil gauge on a valve stem: the air pushes a piston against a spring and the piston pushes the marked bar out; the bar stays out to show the reading.

lines.name: titration
lines.sig: titration cx cy width k=strongstrong|weakstrong deliver=0 lab=1 lit=burette|stopcock|clamp
lines.desc: Alkali from a burette into acid with phenolphthalein: drops flash pink and swirl away until, at 25.00 cm³, the flask stays pale pink.

lines.name: toaster
lines.sig: toaster cx cy width shade=1-6 lab=1
lines.desc: Push the lever: the bread drops between glowing nichrome elements, browns, and pops up when the timer runs out.

lines.name: toilettank
lines.sig: toilettank cx cy height k=ok|running lab=1 lit=flapper|float|overflow|chain|lever|handle
lines.desc: Toilet tank cut open: fill valve and float cup, overflow tube, flapper on its chain to the trip lever and handle. A flush lifts the flapper; the float falls, opens the fill valve, and shuts it at the fill line.

lines.name: toolbox
lines.sig: toolbox cx cy width open=0|1 lab=1 lit=box|lid|latches|tray|tools
lines.desc: A red steel toolbox: the draw-latches flip down, the lid swings back on its piano hinge, and inside are the lift-out tray and the hammer in its well.

lines.name: toothbrush
lines.sig: toothbrush cx cy width paste=0|1 lab=1 lit=handle|bristles|tube|paste
lines.desc: A toothbrush (handle with rubber grip, neck, head with tufts of bristles) and a tube of fluoride paste: a pea-sized blob (about 0.25 g) is enough.

lines.name: toppanbalance
lines.sig: toppanbalance cx cy k load=0..600 tare=0|1 lab=0 lit=body|display|tare|pan|level
lines.desc: A digital top-pan balance (0.01 g, up to 600 g): the display steps to the mass on the pan and settles; TARE zeroes it with a beaker on, so then it reads only what is added. anchors: pan

lines.name: towercooler
lines.sig: towercooler cx cy k spin=0|1 lab=0 lit=base|pipes|fins|fan
lines.desc: A processor tower cooler: copper base, heat pipes up into a tower of aluminium fins, a 120 mm fan clipped on the front; spin=1 turns the fan. anchors: fan top base

lines.name: track
lines.sig: track cx cy width race=0..1 lab=1 lit=runners|kerb|starts|finish|stand
lines.desc: A model of a 400 m running track: four lanes, the kerb and infield, the common finish line and the staggered starts; four runners run a 400 m race.

lines.name: trafficlight
lines.sig: trafficlight cx cy height k=red|redamber|green|amber lab=1 lit=head|button|pole
lines.desc: A UK three-aspect traffic signal on its pole, visors over each lens, with the pedestrian push-button box: red, red and amber, green, amber, red.

lines.name: transformer
lines.sig: transformer cx cy height k=up|down vp=12 lab=1 lit=core|primary|secondary
lines.desc: A bench transformer: laminated iron core, a 200-turn primary and a secondary of 400 (step up) or 100 (step down) turns, with a voltmeter on each side: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np.

lines.name: treaddepth
lines.sig: treaddepth cx cy width k=good|worn lab=1
lines.desc: Tyre tread cut through with a digital depth gauge in the middle groove; its pin goes down to the groove floor and the screen reads the depth, new and worn to the wear bar.

lines.name: tripod
lines.sig: tripod cx cy k gauze=0|1 lab=0 lit=ring|legs|gauze
lines.desc: A steel tripod 20 cm tall with a wire gauze and its ceramic centre on top, to stand a beaker over a Bunsen burner (draw the burner first, at the tripod's origin). anchors: top

lines.name: tubecradle
lines.sig: tubecradle cx cy k lab=0 lit=cradle|pads
lines.desc: A V-cradle (3 × 6 × 6 cm) with cork pads that holds a 3 cm laser tube with its axis 6.1 cm over the board; two of them carry the He-Ne tube. anchors: axis

lines.name: tuningfork
lines.sig: tuningfork cx cy k aim=down|up|flat ring=0..1 lab=0 lit=stem|prongs
lines.desc: A 512 Hz steel tuning fork 15 cm long (stem, yoke, two prongs stamped 512 Hz); struck, its prongs vibrate as a blur that dies away over about ten seconds. anchors: stem tips

lines.name: turbine
lines.sig: turbine cx cy height spin=1 wind=0-30 lab=1 lit=blades|hub|shaft|gearbox|brake|generator|tower
lines.desc: A wind turbine with its nacelle cut open: the blades turn a slow shaft, the gearbox speeds it up about 100 times for the generator, and power climbs with the cube of the wind speed.

lines.name: turntable
lines.sig: turntable cx cy k deg=0..360 h=4..12 prism=0|1 lab=0 lit=base|ring|table|prism
lines.desc: A turning table 10 cm across in a fixed degree ring on a column and foot, with an index that reads its angle; prism=1 carries a 60° glass prism that turns with it; h lifts the top to the beam. anchors: top centre

lines.name: tweeterunit
lines.sig: tweeterunit cx cy k aim=side|front play=0|1 lab=0 lit=faceplate|dome|magnet|terminals
lines.desc: A dome tweeter for the treble: round faceplate, a small soft dome that vibrates, and its little magnet behind. anchors: front back

lines.name: tyrechange
lines.desc: Front corner of a car with its wheel, jack, wrench, spare, hubcap tray and warning triangle; each step is a pose of the same model.

lines.name: usbpowermod
lines.sig: usbpowermod cx cy k on=0|1 lab=0 lit=board|socket|switch|lamp|pins
lines.desc: A breadboard power module: a small green board with a USB socket, a push switch and a lamp, whose pins go into the breadboard's two power rails to feed them 5 V. anchors: plus minus

lines.name: uvlamp
lines.sig: uvlamp cx cy k on=0..1 value=1..100 lab=0 lit=base|hood|tube|note|switch
lines.desc: A small UV fake-note checker, 20 × 15 × 12 cm: a violet UV tube under a hood over a plate with a banknote on it; on lights the tube and the note's hidden strip glows (why real notes are hard to copy). anchors: plate

lines.name: vacuumchamber
lines.sig: vacuumchamber cx cy k lab=0 lit=base|ring|glass|flange|port
lines.desc: The round vacuum chamber of a gold-foil experiment: a bolted steel base with a degree ring on its floor (0° along the beam), a glass wall with a steel flange, and a pump port with a hose barb. anchors: centre rim port

lines.name: vacuumpump
lines.sig: vacuumpump cx cy k on=0|1 lab=0 lit=foot|motor|pump|gauge|switch|inlet
lines.desc: An electric vacuum pump 25 × 12 × 15 cm: a motor on a steel foot with a fan cowl and a rocker switch, the pump block with a barbed inlet on top for the hose, an oil sight glass and a vacuum gauge; on=1 the motor runs and the gauge falls toward −100 kPa. anchors: inlet switch

lines.name: vacuumtube
lines.sig: vacuumtube cx cy k half=all|back|front lab=0 lit=glass|ends|saddles|rail|port
lines.desc: A 60 cm evacuated glass tube, 15 cm across, on two saddles with steel end flanges, a pump arm with a stopcock and a rail inside for the Stern–Gerlach oven, magnet and plate, so the silver atoms fly without hitting air. anchors: floor axis left right port

lines.name: vaultdoor
lines.sig: vaultdoor cx cy k wheel=0..1 retract=0..1 door=0..1 lab=0 lit=frame|door|wheel|dial|bolts|hinge|vault
lines.desc: A round bank vault door, 176 cm across and 40 cm thick, in a 200 × 220 cm steel frame: spoked wheel, combination dial, nine bolts into keepers round the doorway, hinge post and arms; inside, shelves of gold bars and note bundles. wheel turns the wheel, retract draws the bolts, door swings it open. anchors: wheel dial hinge vault

lines.name: vehicle
lines.sig: vehicle cx cy length k=car|bus|train c=red|blue|green|yellow|orange drive=0|1 lift=0..1 lab=1 lit=body|engine|gearbox|shaft|axle|wheel|motor
lines.desc: A car, bus or diesel-electric locomotive, side on: drive it and the wheels turn; lift the body to see how the engine drives them (shaft and differential, or generator, cables and traction motors).

lines.name: velcropad
lines.sig: velcropad cx cy k aim=left|right tilt=-40..40 x=0..200 v=0|1 lab=0 lit=pad|plate|screws
lines.desc: A Velcro hook pad on a backing plate, screwed to a dynamics trolley's front so two trolleys stick together when they collide; rides with the trolley (same tilt, x, v). anchors: face

lines.name: venturitube
lines.sig: venturitube cx cy k flow=0..1 lab=0 lit=pipe|water|supports|flanges
lines.desc: A glass venturi tube 50 cm long, 4 cm across narrowing to 2 cm at the throat, on two wooden saddles, full of water; flow moves tracer specks through it, 4× faster in the throat; three tapping stubs on top for manometer tubes. anchors: t1 t2 t3 in out

lines.name: vial
lines.sig: vial cx cy size k=vial|dose ml=0.1-3 lbl=0 lab=0 lit=vial|stopper|cap|syringe|plunger|needle |text
lines.desc: A 10 mL vial with its rubber stopper and crimp cap; with k=dose a syringe pushes in air equal to the dose, then draws the dose, read at the plunger's front edge.

lines.name: volcano
lines.sig: volcano cx baseY width erupt=0..1 lab=1 lit=chamber|vent|crater|sidevent|flow|layers
lines.desc: A cut-away volcano model: magma rises from the chamber up the main vent, spills from the crater as lava, and ash pours out.

lines.name: walker
lines.sig: walker cx cy height k=walker|crutch h=71-91 (crutch 112-132) roll=cm lab=1 lit=grip|button|wheel|foot|frame
lines.desc: A two-wheeled walking frame: press the spring buttons to slide the legs to a new hole (2.5 cm a step, grips 71–91 cm high), then push it ahead on its front wheels.

lines.name: wallpanel
lines.sig: wallpanel cx cy k w=40..300 h=60..260 see=0|1 lab=0 lit=wall|studs|baseboard
lines.desc: A piece of a painted interior wall: ½ in drywall screwed to 2×4 studs 16 in (40.6 cm) apart, a baseboard along the floor; see=1 shows the studs through it; a part to place in any scene, its face is y = 0. anchors: —

lines.name: wallsocket
lines.sig: wallsocket cx cy k sw=0|1 lab=0 lit=plate|socket|switch|lamp|earth|live|neutral
lines.desc: A switched wall socket plate (Indian 6 A style) 14 × 8.6 cm: three holes with brass spring contacts, the bigger earth hole on top, a switch and a red neon lamp on the left; sw=1 switches it on and lights the lamp. anchors: socket switch

lines.name: wallstuds
lines.sig: wallstuds cx cy width see=0|1 hang=0|1 lab=1 lit=studs|drywall|plates|screws|bracket
lines.desc: A framed wall: 2×4 studs 16 in apart behind the drywall, found by their rows of screw heads; the drywall goes see-through and a shelf bracket is screwed into a stud.

lines.name: wallswitch
lines.sig: wallswitch cx cy k on=0|1 lab=0 lit=plate|toggle
lines.desc: A wall light switch: a bevelled cover plate with two screws, the toggle up for on, down for off; set({ on }) flips it with a snap.

lines.name: warntriangle
lines.sig: warntriangle cx cy size open=0|1 lit=triangle|stand lab=1
lines.desc: Red reflective warning triangle on its folding stand: the arms swing up and clip, the legs swing out, the triangle stands up.

lines.name: washer
lines.sig: washer cx cy height spin=0|1 lab=1 lit=drum|door|drawer|dial|filter
lines.desc: A front-loader: at 50 rpm the lifters raise the clothes and drop them through the water; at 1200 rpm they are pinned to the drum wall and the water is flung out through its holes.

lines.name: wastewater
lines.sig: wastewater cx cy width labels=1 step=1..5 lit=screen|settling|aeration|blower|clarifier|river
lines.desc: A cut-away model of a sewage works: screen, primary settling, aeration with bubbles, round clarifier with a turning bridge, and the outfall to the river.

lines.name: watchcradle
lines.sig: watchcradle cx cy k lab=0 lit=base|blocks|felt
lines.desc: A small walnut display cradle 8 × 4 × 3 cm: a base and two felt-lined blocks cut to one curve, the seat a stopwatch stands upright in. anchors: seat top

lines.name: waterglass
lines.sig: waterglass cx cy height level=0-100 lab=1 lit=glass|water|jug|bubbles
lines.desc: A glass tumbler of water on a coaster: set a higher level and the jug tips and pours until the water reaches it; the millilitres are the glass's real volume.

lines.name: waterheater
lines.sig: waterheater cx cy height tap=0|1 lab=1 lit=tank|diptube|burner|tp|drain|anode|flue
lines.desc: A gas tank water heater cut open: cold water goes down the dip tube to the bottom, hot leaves from the top, and the burner lights when the thermostat feels the cold coming up.

lines.name: watertap
lines.sig: watertap cx cy k reach=6..30 drop=5..60 open=0|1 lab=0 lit=pipe|tap|handle|water
lines.desc: A bench water tap: a steel riser 40 cm tall and an arm to a brass quarter-turn tap, its spout pointing down; open it (lever along the pipe) and water runs into the can or sink under it. anchors: spout top

lines.name: watertray
lines.sig: watertray cx cy k w=30..100 water=0..1 lab=0 lit=tray|water
lines.desc: A long shallow plastic tray (60 × 20 × 4 cm) with a rolled lip and a drain spout, lying along x, holding a little water; catches the jets from a spouting can. anchors: inside rim

lines.name: watertreat
lines.sig: watertreat cx cy width labels=1 step=1..6 lit=intake|flocculation|settling|filter|chlorine|storage|tap
lines.desc: A cut-away model of a water treatment works: intake, flocculation, settling, sand filter, chlorine, storage and tap; each step lets the water into the next stage and it clears.

lines.name: wellring
lines.sig: wellring cx cy k lab=0 lit=stones|coping|inside
lines.desc: A stone well ring 60 cm across and 46 cm high: four courses of stones in a running bond, a coping of ten slabs, the dark opening with the inside wall going down. anchors: rim

lines.name: wheelaxle
lines.sig: wheelaxle cx cy size load=2 lab=1
lines.desc: A windlass over a well: the big wheel and small drum turn together, so a small effort on the rim lifts a heavy bucket.

lines.name: wheelchair
lines.sig: wheelchair cx cy size roll=cm brake=0|1 lab=1 lit=wheel|pushrim|caster|brake|footrest|seat
lines.desc: A manual wheelchair: push the rims and the 61 cm rear wheels roll it 1.92 m a turn; push the brake levers forward and the shoes lock the tyres.

lines.name: whitecard
lines.sig: whitecard cx cy k w=10..40 d=8..30 posts=0|1 hole=none|wire|coil lab=0 lit=card|posts
lines.desc: A stiff white card 22 × 14 cm to plot a magnetic field on: lies on the bench, or stands 5.6 cm up on four brass posts with a hole for a wire or two rows of holes for a coil. anchors: top

lines.name: whitescreen
lines.sig: whitescreen cx cy k w=10..30 h=8..20 cz=6..40 rider=0|1 x=-70..70 show=blank|patch|shadow|fringes|rings size=0.2..12 shift=0..20 c=red|green|amber|white lab=0 lit=screen|stand|light
lines.example: whitescreen 470 470 14 w=24 h=15 cz=14 rider=1 show=patch size=3 c=amber lab=1
lines.desc: A white viewing screen on a stand or on its own optical bench rider: it shows a light patch, a shadow, two-slit fringes or circular fringes, and slides along the bench. anchors: centre top

lines.name: whitetile
lines.sig: whitetile cx cy k w=4..30 d=4..30 lab=0 lit=tile
lines.desc: A white glazed tile laid on the bench under a flask or a test tube so a colour change shows clearly; w × d in cm (11.6 × 10.4 by default). anchors: top

lines.name: wifirouter
lines.sig: wifirouter cx cy k on=0|1 lid=0..1 ant=0..90 lab=0 lit=tray|lid|board|soc|wifi|ports|antenna|leds
lines.desc: A Wi-Fi router 22 × 15 × 4 cm: white case on rubber feet, lid with vents and four lights, inside the board with processor and heatsink, two radio cans, five network jacks; on=1 lights and flickers it and radio waves spread, lid=1 lifts the lid off, ant= folds the antennas. anchors: top power

lines.name: winch
lines.sig: winch cx cy k wind=0..100 lab=0 lit=bracket|drum|crank|string
lines.desc: A small hand winch on a bracket: a wooden drum between flanges, a ratchet and pawl, a crank; winding it turns the drum and the string's coil grows (wind = cm of string pulled in). anchors: string

lines.name: windlass
lines.sig: windlass cx cy k turns=0..6 rope=0..120 lab=0 lit=frame|drum|wheel|handle|rope
lines.desc: A windlass: two oak posts carry a steel axle with a small drum (r 3 cm) the rope winds on and a big handwheel (R 13 cm) with a crank handle; turning the handle winds the rope in, so a small effort lifts a load 4.3 times bigger. anchors: hook drum handle top

lines.name: windtunnel
lines.sig: windtunnel cx cy width aoa=0-18 lab=1 lit=wing|fan|honeycomb|balance
lines.desc: A wind tunnel: honeycomb inlet, contraction, glass test section with a wing on a lift balance, diffuser and fan; smoke streams bend over the wing, and the lift rises with the angle until the wing stalls.

lines.name: wiper
lines.sig: wiper cx cy width sweep=0-1 lift=0-1 lab=1
lines.desc: Wiper arm on its pivot with the spring, hinge and nut cover; blade with its rubber edge and release tab; it sweeps the wet glass, then lifts off it.

lines.name: wirefield
lines.sig: wirefield cx cy size k=wire|solenoid I=5 lab=1 lit=wire|coil|compasses|supply
lines.desc: Plotting compasses on a card round a current-carrying wire (field in circles, B = μ₀I/2πr) or a solenoid (like a bar magnet, B = μ₀nI inside).

lines.name: wirelead
lines.sig: wirelead cx cy k to=<id>.<anchor> dx=-200..200 dy=-200..200 dz=-200..200 c=red|black|blue|green|yellow sag=0..1 flow=0|1 lab=0 lit=wire|clips
lines.example: wirelead 250 300 26 dx=22 dy=-4 dz=0 c=red sag=0.5
lines.desc: An insulated test lead with a crocodile clip on each end (serrated jaws, spring, coloured boot), hanging in a soft curve from its start to to=<id>.<anchor> (or dx dy dz cm); flow=1 runs small dots along it for the current. anchors: end

lines.name: woodblock
lines.sig: woodblock cx cy k kind=float|pull tilt=-40..40 x=0..200 v=0|1 mu=0.1..0.9 water=0|1 lab=0 lit=block|eye
lines.desc: A wooden block: a 6 × 4 × 3.5 cm pine block that floats 60 % under and bobs into place, or a 10 × 6 × 6 cm beech block with a screw eye that sticks on a slope while tan θ ≤ μ, then slides at g(sin θ − μk cos θ). anchors: top eye

lines.name: woodchair
lines.sig: woodchair cx cy k wobble=0..1 fix=0..1 over=0|1 lab=0 lit=seat|back|legs|joint
lines.desc: A wooden kitchen chair, seat 45 cm high, its seat held by a screwed corner block at each corner; wobble opens the front-left leg's joint, over=1 turns it upside down (seat on the floor, the corner block facing up) and fix drives its corner-block screw home to close it; a part to place in any scene. anchors: joint seat

lines.name: woodscrew
lines.sig: woodscrew cx cy k aim=wall|down|up in=0..1 lab=0 lit=screw
lines.desc: A 5 cm wood screw: gimlet point, coarse thread, smooth shank, countersunk head with a cross (Phillips) recess; in=0 its point on the surface, in=1 driven home; set({ in }) turns it in. anchors: head

lines.name: woodsupport
lines.sig: woodsupport cx cy k lab=0 lit=block
lines.desc: A small pine block 4 cm wide and 4 cm tall with a round notch in its top, so a 1 cm bolt or rod lying along x rests in it; two of them hold an electromagnet's bolt above the bench. anchors: cradle

lines.name: woodtuberack
lines.sig: woodtuberack cx cy k n=2..12 c=red,blue,green,yellow shelf=1|0 lab=0 lit=rack|tubes
lines.desc: A wooden test-tube rack with a drilled top shelf, a middle shelf, end posts and drying pegs, holding 16 mm test tubes of coloured liquids (or empty holes); a bench part. anchors: hole1 hole2 hole3 … (the bench point under each hole, where a tube's bottom stands) top

lines.name: wooferunit
lines.sig: wooferunit cx cy k aim=side|front cut=0|1 play=0|1 lab=0 lit=basket|surround|cone|spider|coil|magnet
lines.desc: A loudspeaker woofer driver: steel basket with four screw holes, rubber surround, paper cone and dust cap, the spider, and the ferrite magnet; cut it to see the voice coil in the magnet's gap, play it and the cone moves in and out. anchors: front back

lines.name: workglove
lines.sig: workglove cx cy k aim=flat|up lab=0 lit=glove
lines.desc: A yellow household rubber glove, 30 cm long: flared cuff with a rolled bead, palm and fingers with a raised diamond grip; lying flat or flat against a wall; a part to place in any scene.

lines.name: worktable
lines.sig: worktable cx cy k w=60..160 d=40..90 wobble=0|1 lab=0 lit=top|legs|apron
lines.desc: A plain wooden work table 75 cm tall: glued-up top, apron, four legs on felt glides and corner blocks; wobble=1 makes one front leg 0.8 cm short so it rocks; a part to place in any scene. anchors: top

lines.name: xlrcable
lines.sig: xlrcable cx cy k to=<id>.<anchor> dx=-200..200 dy=-200..200 dz=-200..200 sag=0..1 lab=0 lit=cable|plugs
lines.example: xlrcable 300 170 20 dx=26 dy=-4 dz=-12 sag=0.5 lab=1
lines.desc: A microphone cable: a female XLR plug pointing up (it goes on under a microphone) and a black cable hanging in a soft curve to a male XLR plug at to=<id>.<anchor> (or dx dy dz cm). anchors: end

lines.name: zoomlens
lines.sig: zoomlens cx cy k f=2.8..16 lab=0 lit=barrel|glass|aperture|mount
lines.desc: An interchangeable zoom lens cut in half: mount, zoom and focus rings, five glass elements in retaining rings and an iris whose seven blades close as the f-number grows. anchors: mount front

lines.name: magnet
lines.sig: magnet cx cy length k=bar|horseshoe lines=0 rot=deg
lines.desc: bar or horseshoe magnet, red N, blue S, field lines; flow moves them

lines.name: cell

lines.desc: battery cell with + and −, or its circuit symbol

lines.name: switch

lines.name: resistor

lines.name: lever

lines.name: wheelaxle
lines.desc: wheel and axle lifting a bucket, effort arrow; flow moves rope; lab=0 hides its words

els.t_final: text 250 42 s=32 | sun behind you + rain in front = rainbow!

steps.say: A rainbow needs two things: sunlight, and raindrops in the air.
Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of every colour.
When light enters a raindrop, it bends, and each colour bends a little differently.
Then it bounces off the back of the drop.
And it comes out spread into a fan of colours.
Millions of drops do this at the same time, so we see a giant arc of colour.
That is why a rainbow appears when the sun is behind you and the rain is in front of you.

els.title: text 60 62 s=44 | Interest on interest
els.note: text 520 100 s=26 f=#2f7fd6 | blue line = simple interest
els.extra: text 300 140 s=30 | extra $59 = interest on interest!

steps.say: Compound interest means you earn interest on your interest, too.
Say you put one hundred dollars in a bank that pays ten percent a year.
After one year you earn ten dollars, so you have one hundred and ten.
The next year, ten percent of one hundred and ten is eleven dollars, not ten. Your interest earned interest.
Keep going, and the growth speeds up. After ten years you have about two hundred and fifty nine dollars.
With simple interest you would only have two hundred. The extra fifty nine dollars is interest on interest.

whiteboard.q: How does the internet send a message?

els.fast: text 330 525 s=32 | ...all in less than a second!

steps.say: When you send a message, your computer does not send it in one piece.
First it cuts the message into small numbered pieces, called packets.
Each packet hops through routers, which pass it toward your friend's address.
Packets can take different roads, so they may arrive in any order.
Your friend's phone puts them back in order using the numbers, and the message appears.
All of this happens in less than a second!

whiteboard.q: How do plants make food? (illustrated recipes)

els.title: title | Leaf captures energy
els.co2: flow 70 385 300 330 c=sky n=2 dots=1 | Carbon dioxide
els.sugar: trail 520 338 560 414 c=orange | Sugar, food for growth

steps.say: Plants make their own food, and the kitchen is the leaf.
Sunlight gives the leaf its energy.
Water travels up from the roots.
Carbon dioxide comes in from the air.
With sunlight's energy, the leaf turns water and carbon dioxide into sugar, its food.
And it breathes out oxygen, the air we need.
Water on Earth is always on the move, in a giant loop called the water cycle.
The sun warms the sea, and water rises into the air as invisible vapour. That is evaporation.
High up, the vapour cools into tiny droplets that gather into clouds. That is condensation.
When the droplets get heavy, they fall as rain or snow. That is precipitation.
Rivers carry the water back to the sea, and the whole cycle starts again.

whiteboard.q: How does the heart pump blood?

els.title: title | The heart: a double pump
els.bodyIn: flow 90 300 318 300 c=blue n=2 | From the body
els.toLungs: flow 408 150 230 182 c=blue at=end | To the lungs
els.fromLungs: flow 870 300 642 300 c=red n=2 | From the lungs
els.toBody: flow 600 172 800 110 c=red at=end | To the body
els.lbl1: label 120 505 c=blue s=24 | Its right side → lungs
els.lbl2: label 610 505 c=red s=24 | Its left side → body

steps.say: Your heart is a pump about the size of your fist, and it never stops.
Used blood, low on oxygen, comes back from the body into its right side.
The right side pumps it to the lungs, where it picks up fresh oxygen.
Fresh blood comes back from the lungs into the left side.
And the strong left side pumps it out to the whole body. Two pumps beating together, about seventy times a minute.
